residualObservations.title: The retain suite reads one external absolute path that is neither manifested nor hash-pinned
residualObservations.detail: That control does .read_text() on /tmp/opensip-design-corrections/grok-application-successor-preparation.v2/prepared/retain-application-review.successor.v1.py to assert the original retainer still has the rglob defect. The path exists in this runtime and the control passes, but it is not in the v3 manifest and carries no pinned digest, unlike the public-custody-before-compaction.v1 counterexample fixture which v3 correctly bundled and hashes. If that path were ever absent the suite would raise FileNotFoundError; prepare-validation asserts returncode 0, so staging fails closed rather than silently skipping. This is the same class of dependency as the original F6, whose path turned out to actually be missing.
residualObservations.evidence: scratch/w02_g1.py external: exists true, isFile true, inV3Manifest false.
residualObservations.optionalRemedy: Bundle that file alongside public-custody-before-compaction.v1 and pin its digest, or assert the expected digest before reading. Offered as optional hardening consistent with how the other counterexample is already handled; not required for this verdict.

residualObservations.title: A Claude reviewer authoring a file whose name equals launch.stdoutName would have it replaced by the sanitized envelope
residualObservations.detail: Correct and intended precedence - the stdout rule must beat the G1 exemption - but it means an authored summary.json would be excluded and the sanitized envelope written under that same name if stdoutName were also summary.json. Reaching this requires a deliberate launch misconfiguration: the launcher's Claude default is response.json, and the exclusion is declared in custody.excludedPrivateSources either way.
residualObservations.optionalRemedy: None needed. If desired, refuse at launch when stdoutName collides with a plausible authored report name. Explicitly not a requirement.

limitations: This is a bounded read-only tooling follow-up review. It is not a final application ACCEPT, not design/blind/source acceptance, and awards no grade.

No application, receipt binding, freeze of a real package, launch, retention of a real review, or activation was performed. All fixtures were synthetic and disposable; every write stayed under this runtime's scratch/ and per-case temporary directories.

G3 was verified as a BOUNDED GUARD EXECUTION. The full application root is absent, so a minimal synthetic stage satisfied freeze's earlier preconditions in order to reach the new block. This is not an end-to-end freeze of a real application package and is not claimed as one.

G2's second check at line 480 was verified statically and by a side-by-side expression differential using the assembler's own helper definitions; it was NOT reached by execution, because line 480 sits after the draft and source-delta stages that require fixtures absent from these inputs. The pre-output check at line 124 WAS executed.

assemble-records.successor.v1.py, prepare-validation.py and verify-applied.py were again not executed end to end for the same reason. prepare-validation's new argument list was verified by complete diff and by executing the resulting suite invocation directly.

The 69 retain and 35 envelope control counts are my own re-measurement from these inputs. Root's separate claim of 15 focused controls was not supplied to me and is neither confirmed nor disputed here.
The four public-custody-before-compaction.v1 fixture files are unchanged historical counterexamples; they were hashed and executed as the suite's contrast case, not line-reviewed.

No Grok or Claude CLI was run, no ~/.grok or ~/.claude session directory was read, and no real private log or reasoning content of any kind was accessed. Every sentinel was an invented synthetic string.
That the failed initial preparation launched no Claude process is attested by preparation-failure.md and is not independently verifiable from these inputs.

In-process module probes ran under host python3 3.14.6 with -B; subprocess suites and guard executions ran under the reference interpreter /tmp/opensip-architecture-review-env/bin/python -I -B. The two were not exhaustively cross-run.
All 32 product qualification gates remain unperformed and condition 5 remains NOT MET. Design acceptance is a separate question this review does not reach.
